name: kernel_density_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, institutional TWAP and VWAP algorithms executing multi-hour directional mandates repeatedly transact at the same price bands within any given 10-minute window, creating high-density clusters in the Gaussian KDE of recent 5-second closes. These KDE modes act as mechanical support/resistance: when NIFTY approaches a high-density mode from above with short-term RSI exhausted below 40, residual buy algorithms still working their orders at that level absorb the incoming sell flow and produce a 10-20 spot-point bounce. The same logic applies in reverse at resistance modes (RSI > 60, approaching from below), where sellers who accumulated near that band provide friction against further advance. At 5-second resolution we enter as proximity to the mode tightens to within 0.1% of price, capturing the first 1-2 bars of bounce before the level either holds or breaks.

indicators.name: kde_modes
indicators.formula: GaussianKDE(close[-120:], bandwidth=silverman) -> local maxima of density evaluated on 60-point grid
indicators.purpose: 120 bars = 10 minutes of 5-second closes. NOT the original 2-hour window (1440 bars). For scalping 30-90 second bounces, we need modes from the current intraday micro-session — levels formed 2 hours ago have been displaced by new information. 10-minute KDE captures the price clustering visible to same-session institutional algos still working their orders.

indicators.name: nearest_support
indicators.formula: argmax(kde_modes[kde_modes < close]) — highest KDE mode strictly below current close
indicators.purpose: The closest high-density price level below current price — represents the nearest zone where residual buy orders cluster. 'Nearest' because KDE can have multiple modes and only the closest is actionable in 30-90 seconds.

indicators.name: nearest_resistance
indicators.formula: argmin(kde_modes[kde_modes > close]) — lowest KDE mode strictly above current close
indicators.purpose: Mirror of nearest_support — closest supply zone above current price.

indicators.name: mode_strength
indicators.formula: kde_density_at_mode / mean(kde_density_over_grid) — relative density at the mode
indicators.purpose: Filters weak/shallow KDE peaks. A mode with strength < 1.5x mean density is not a meaningful cluster; it could just be a local noise peak in a thin distribution. Strength >= 1.5 indicates the level has received significantly above-average price concentration.

indicators.name: rsi_36
indicators.purpose: 36 bars = 3-minute RSI. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min = 14-minute RSI. For 5-second bars holding 30-90 seconds, we want a 3-minute RSI to detect short-term momentum exhaustion near the KDE mode. Faster RSI (e.g., 12 bars) is too noisy at 5s resolution; 36 bars smooths enough to give a meaningful overbought/oversold reading in the context of a KDE mode approach.

conditions: close > nearest_support (price above support, not yet broken)
rsi_36 < 40 (short-term momentum exhausted — oversold into support)
buy_ce.confirmation: VIX < 22 (S/R levels unreliable in high-vol when index behaves erratically)

conditions: close < nearest_resistance (price below resistance, not yet broken)

exit.stop_rationale: A 4-point adverse option move (~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5) signals the KDE mode has failed — price has moved meaningfully through the level rather than bouncing. For 30-90 second NIFTY holds, a 8 spot-point level break is decisive: the support/resistance is confirmed absent and the thesis is wrong.
exit.target_rationale: A bounce from a meaningful NIFTY KDE support/resistance mode should produce 12-15 spot points of reversion as resting institutional orders absorb the flow. 6 option points (~12 spot points at delta 0.5) captures the lower bound of expected bounce amplitude while maintaining a 1:1.5 R:R. This is consistent with 30-second NIFTY typical moves of 2-5 option pts — we target the upper end given the KDE signal provides higher conviction.

filters.vix_filter: VIX < 22 — above 22, intraday NIFTY moves become gappy and erratic, KDE modes from calm periods are overrun by momentum; original also used VIX < 22
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST — start at 09:30 to ensure 120-bar (10-min) warmup since 09:20 before first signal
filters.volume_filter: None — NIFTY volume is inherently noisy at 5s; mode strength filter replaces volume filter
filters.trend_filter: Implicit — RSI < 40 or RSI > 60 ensures we're not chasing a strongly trending bar
filters.spread_filter: None — limit orders, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — KDE S/R is a rigorous version of subjective S/R; the statistical approach is cleaner but the underlying concept (price memory at clustered levels) is well-known and arbitrageable. Edge decays as more algos detect the same KDE modes.

adaptation_notes: Three major changes from the original equity strategy: (1) Lookback compressed from 120 bars × 1-min = 2 hours to 120 bars × 5s = 10 minutes, because NIFTY intraday S/R relevant for 30-90s scalping lives in the recent micro-session, not the full morning session. (2) RSI period changed from RSI(14, 1-min) = 14 min to RSI(36, 5s) = 3 min — faster exhaustion detection appropriate for 5-second bars. (3) Short-selling replaced with buy_pe (ATM put options) — no directional short constraint on options.
weaknesses: KDE computed fresh each bar is computationally intensive — mitigated by vectorized numpy but Python loop overhead still exists
Silverman bandwidth assumes near-Gaussian price distribution — NIFTY intraday prices can be bimodal after major gap events, producing spurious modes
In strong trending sessions (e.g., post-RBI policy), KDE modes shift rapidly, making the lookback window stale mid-session
RSI < 40 near support is rare on NIFTY intraday (index rarely oversells without fast recovery) — trade frequency may be low
